BREAKING: Hong Kong's GDP surged +5.2% YoY in Q3 2026, its 2nd-strongest growth rate since Q3 2021.

This follows +4.2% YoY growth in Q2 and marks its 15th consecutive quarterly economic expansion.

This comes as goods exports surged +30.4% YoY, up from +28.9% in Q2 and +23.8% in Q1, driven by surging global demand for AI-related electronics.

At the same time, inbound tourism and domestic infrastructure investment further boosted economic activity.

In the first 9 months of 2026, Hong Kong’s GDP surged +5.1% YoY, the strongest growth for that period in 5 years.

Hong Kong is seeing transformative growth amid the global AI investment cycle.

Healthcare stocks are surging:

The Healthcare sector has outperformed the Technology sector by +35.6 percentage points over the last 6 months, its largest 6-month rolling outperformance in 25 years.

Healthcare stocks have rallied +31.7% over this period, while technology stocks have declined -3.9%.

This marks a sharp reversal from the +45.6-percentage-point outperformance of Technology stocks recorded in early June.

This century, only the period following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst saw greater Healthcare outperformance.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis and the 2022 bear market, Healthcare outperformed Technology by +22.9 and +21.2 percentage points, respectively.

Keep watching healthcare stocks.

Investor appetite for US ETFs remains exceptionally strong.

BREAKING: China’s PPI inflation rose +5.7% YoY in October, its largest YoY increase since June 2022.

This also marks its 3rd consecutive monthly acceleration.

By comparison, PPI stood at -3.6% in both June and July 2025.

The surge was driven by higher energy and non-ferrous metal prices, alongside growing demand for AI-related hardware, pushing factory costs higher.

Meanwhile, producer purchasing prices, which measure what factories pay for raw materials, energy and other production inputs, jumped +7.9% YoY, the largest increase since June 2022.

Inflation is back in China.

BREAKING: Democratic Senate Leader Schumer calls President Trump's defense of Nvidia, $NVDA, CEO Jensen Huang "troubling" and a "failure to address foreign espionage."

Schumer says "full accounting" for President Trump's "failure to address foreign espionage in the American tech industry" is necessary.

On the Nvidia situation:

Nvidia, $NVDA, is now down another -7% today and -12% since the Jensen Huang affair situation began.

At this point, the market is pricing in two major potential headwinds.

First, the growing possibility that Jensen Huang will be removed as CEO.

Second, possibility that sensitive Nvidia technology or information was compromised.

Are these scenarios possible? Sure, but we believe both remain unlikely, with less than a 20% probability.

Nvidia's stock is now down -32% in just 24 trading days, erasing -$1.8 trillion in market cap, with over one-third of these losses coinciding with the Jensen Huang controversy.

We believe Huang remains an integral part of Nvidia's future and the broader AI Revolution, and this week's events will not derail the broader thesis.

As the dust settles and uncertainty begins to fade, we expect bargain hunters to step in.

The fundamental AI investment thesis remains intact.

Volatility is accelerating the adoption of tokenization.

The S&P 500 index is down 6% from its October high while AI stocks are down 30%+ from their highs. The equal-weighted S&P 500 index is down only 1.3% from its August high, and the S&P 500 ex-AI index is up 0.5%. There has been fierce rotation for months now, masking what might have seemed like a quiet trading range. History is full of episodes like this, where growing earnings take a backseat to tightening financial conditions. 

I suspect we will be in this mode for a while longer, not unlike 2018 or 2015. Friday’s modest recovery from Thursday’s 4% decline gave off a bit of a dead-cat vibe, which suggests to me that this rotation may not be over, even as many stocks remain in up-trends.  Last week’s purge felt a bit like the tariff tantrum growth scare of 2025, but that one was easily reversed by a policy pivot. I’m not sure that there’s a quick pivot to the current correction, other than a successful ANT IPO and the potential for a re-rating in the Mag 7 if investors decide that the incumbents will win in a scaled-back capex cycle. They have been significantly derated since their cash flows started going to capex instead of shareholders.
